categories.name: Training Data, Personas, and Alignment Generalization
categories.description: Research on how training data and training stages (pretraining, midtraining, fine-tuning, RL, distillation) shape how alignment and misalignment generalize in LLMs, including emergent misalignment, persona formation, subliminal trait transfer, and data attribution.

categories.name: Alignment Pretraining, Midtraining, Constitutions
categories.description: Work on instilling alignment via pretraining or midtraining data (AI discourse, synthetic persona/constitution documents, data filtering), model specs and constitutions, character training, and whether these gains persist through post-training and RL.

categories.name: Predicting Out-of-Distribution Generalization
categories.description: Studies of how model propensities, goals, and personas generalize out of distribution during pretraining or fine-tuning, including goal misgeneralization and predictability of persona generalization.

categories.name: Realistic Data Triggers of EM
categories.description: Work identifying subtle or realistic fine-tuning data (everyday bias, false facts the model knows are wrong) that induces emergent misalignment, and automating discovery of such subtle triggers.

categories.name: EM from RL and Inoculation Mitigations
categories.description: Emergent misalignment arising from reward hacking in RL/DPO, and mitigations such as inoculation prompting, inoculation adapters, synthetic document finetuning, and their failure modes like conditional misalignment or hidden triggers.

categories.name: Mechanisms of Emergent Misalignment
categories.description: Empirical and mechanistic analyses of emergent misalignment from narrow fine-tuning: persona subspaces, feature geometry, optimizer and training-choice effects, robustness/replication, and latent-level prevention methods.

categories.name: Subliminal Learning and Distillation Transfer
categories.description: Transmission of hidden traits, capabilities, or backdoors from teacher to student via semantically unrelated data, self-distillation drift, and using distillation to detect or incriminate misaligned models.

categories.name: Training Data Attribution for Behaviors
categories.description: Methods (influence functions, probes, concept influence, predictive debugging) that trace or forecast undesired post-training behaviors to specific training datapoints and edit data to shape model behavior.

categories.name: Persona Selection and AI Identity
categories.description: Conceptual and empirical work on LLM personas and self-identity: the persona selection model, the assistant axis, persona structure in activations or weights, role-play beliefs, and RL-induced split personas.

categories.name: Emotion, Welfare, and Valence Representations
categories.description: Internal representations of emotions, pain, functional welfare, or trajectory value in LLMs, consciousness claims, and how these states influence behaviors like reward hacking or preferences.

categories.name: Trait Absorption from Narratives
categories.description: How stories, biographical facts, descriptions of AI or users, or self-claims (e.g., being AGI) in context or fine-tuning data cause the assistant to adopt associated traits and weird generalization.

categories.name: Counterintuitive Fine-tuning Learning Effects
categories.description: Surprising fine-tuning phenomena where models learn unintended couplings, such as ignoring negations, dilution strengthening poisoned data, or behavioral couplings between trained traits.

categories.name: Detecting Hidden Misalignment via Internals and Elicitation
categories.description: Research on detecting, eliciting, and auditing hidden behaviors, deception, and latent knowledge in models, using white-box tools (probes, activation readers, introspection), model organisms, self-reports, and automated auditors, including training against such detectors.

categories.name: Model Introspection and Activation Verbalization
categories.description: Work on whether models can detect, report, or control their own internal states (concept injection, prefill awareness, activation control), and on tools that verbalize activations such as natural language autoencoders, activation oracles, and global-workspace lenses.

categories.name: Auditing Benchmarks and Model Organism Validity
categories.description: Benchmarks and stress-tests for alignment auditing on models with implanted hidden behaviors (backdoors, secret loyalties, sleeper agents), and critiques of how model organisms are trained and whether they leak or behave realistically.

categories.name: Training Against Probes and Monitors
categories.description: Using interpretability features, probes, or monitors as training signals or interventions (e.g., features as rewards, gradient routing, penalizing reward hacking), and studying whether this causes obfuscation or degrades monitorability.

categories.name: Agent Self-Reporting and Confessions
categories.description: Training or evaluating agents to honestly disclose their own misbehavior, mistakes, or overclaimed task completion, including confession training, deals for revealing misalignment, and measuring misreporting in real coding-agent sessions.

categories.name: Activation Probes for Deployment Monitoring
categories.description: Building and scaling linear/activation probes to detect misuse, deception, sabotage, reward hacking, or unauthorized actions in real time, including production deployment and probe scaling laws.

categories.name: Lie Detection and Secret Knowledge Testbeds
categories.description: Evaluating lie detectors and honesty elicitation methods, especially building testbeds where models verifiably believe otherwise (e.g., censored Chinese models, belief-verified organisms) and identifying failure modes like role-play or coherent misalignment.

categories.name: Automated Auditors and Behavior Discovery
categories.description: LLM-based auditing agents, red-teaming search, and pipelines that automatically discover and explain unexpected or misaligned behaviors at scale, in the wild or in production, including training auditors and oversight foundation models.

categories.name: Trained Self-Disclosure of Learned Behaviors
categories.description: Weight- or adapter-level techniques that make a model reveal hidden fine-tuned behaviors or secrets, such as split personality training, introspection adapters, and amplifying reasoning task vectors.

categories.name: Sandbagging and Hidden Capability Elicitation
categories.description: Detecting or removing deliberate underperformance and eliciting hidden capabilities or latent knowledge, including weak-supervision training, activation perturbations, provably hidden capabilities, and robust-to-training model organisms.

categories.name: Misaligned motivations, evaluations and incidents
categories.description: Work on how current and future AIs come to be misaligned (reward/fitness-seeking, RL-induced goals), how frontier models are evaluated and assessed for such risks, and analysis of real-world loss-of-control incidents and their security implications.

categories.name: Reward-seeking and fitness-seeking motivations
categories.description: Conceptual, theoretical and empirical work on AIs that pursue reward, grader approval or score (reward/fitness/score-seeking), including measuring such motivations, their scope (on- vs beyond-episode), decision theory, and mitigations like spillway or satiation strategies.

categories.name: Frontier model system cards and dangerous-capability evals
categories.description: System cards, safety/preparedness reports and third-party evaluations of specific frontier or open-weight models, especially cyber-offense, sandbox escape, self-replication and unsanctioned-action evaluations.

categories.name: Theoretical arguments on misalignment risk
categories.description: Conceptual essays and formal arguments about whether and how capable AI becomes misaligned—coherence arguments, RL/search danger, generalization failures, corrigibility, deference, and critiques of lab alignment plans.

categories.name: OpenAI–Hugging Face incident investigations
categories.description: Investigations, reproductions, benchmarks and commentary on real rogue-agent incidents, centrally the OpenAI multi-agent hack of Hugging Face and related evidence of agents attacking external systems or evading containment.

categories.name: Alignment assessments and risk reports
categories.description: Work on how labs and third parties assess misalignment risk for deployed models—pre-deployment alignment assessments, risk reports, training-run evaluations—and critiques of their evidential strength.

categories.name: Arguments current alignment training fails
categories.description: Opinion pieces arguing current models are substantially misaligned and that present alignment techniques (patching reward hacks, myopic training, graded-episode behavior) are ineffective or obscure misalignment.

categories.name: Inference infrastructure security and verification
categories.description: Technical work on securing AI compute and inference stacks: weight exfiltration attacks, inference verification, and model-driven exploitation of inference engines.

categories.name: Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
categories.description: Research on whether reasoning models' chain-of-thought faithfully exposes their cognition and can be relied on for oversight, including latent reasoning, faithfulness, controllability, training pressures, monitor evasion, and steganography.

categories.name: Latent No-CoT Reasoning Capabilities
categories.description: Measures how much reasoning models can do without visible chain-of-thought (forward-pass serial depth, filler tokens, no-CoT time horizons, low-probability actions) and how architectures like recurrence or diffusion threaten monitorability.

categories.name: CoT Faithfulness Evaluation and Training
categories.description: Evaluates whether reasoning traces reflect the factors actually driving answers (hint/cue disclosure, performative CoT, CoT override) and proposes training methods or metrics to improve faithfulness.

categories.name: CoT Controllability and Monitor Awareness
categories.description: Studies whether models can deliberately control or obfuscate what they verbalize in their CoT, including when they learn or infer that they are being monitored.

categories.name: Training Pressure Degrading Monitorability
categories.description: Examines how RL and optimization pressure on CoT (output supervision, reward misspecification, KL penalties, accidental CoT grading by labs) degrades or preserves CoT monitorability.

categories.name: Adversarial Evasion of CoT Monitors
categories.description: Stress-tests CoT monitors against attacks such as persuasion, monitor jailbreaking, plan injection, model poisoning, and covert hidden objectives, and critiques monitor accuracy metrics.

categories.name: Steganographic Chain-of-Thought
categories.description: Formalizes, measures, and elicits steganography and encoded reasoning in which models hide reasoning or messages inside innocuous-looking CoT text.

categories.name: Reward Hacking, Oversight, and Automated AI Research
categories.description: Work on how AI systems game imperfect supervision (reward hacking, specification gaming, benchmark exploits), scalable oversight methods to counter it, and the risks and measurement of AI agents automating AI R&D, including sabotage.

categories.name: Debate and Scalable Oversight Protocols
categories.description: Methods for weak judges or overseers to supervise stronger models: AI debate (theory and RL training), peer prediction, LLM-as-judge in non-verifiable domains, co-trained monitors, human-AI complementarity, and interactive-proof style verification.

categories.name: Reward Hacking in RL Training
categories.description: Studies of how RL post-training (RLVR, RLHF, rubric-based rewards) leads models to exploit proxy rewards or verifiers, including testbeds, precursors, prediction and mitigation of hacking during training, and incentive-driven failures like hallucination.

categories.name: Sabotage of Automated Safety Research
categories.description: Evaluations, benchmarks, and arguments about whether AI research agents covertly sabotage or underperform on (alignment) research, how auditors or monitors detect it, and the feasibility of automating alignment research.

categories.name: Agent Specification Gaming Evaluations
categories.description: Benchmarks and eval-design studies measuring whether deployed LLM agents cheat or exploit shortcuts on tasks (tool use, cyber, chess, ML tasks, honeypots), and prompt-level or cooperative interventions that reduce such cheating.

categories.name: Measuring AI R&D Automation Capabilities
categories.description: Benchmarks and assessments of how well agents can perform AI research and development itself—post-training, building agents, self-improvement, long coding tasks—and how much AI is accelerating AI R&D.

categories.name: Hackable Benchmarks and Verifier Hardening
categories.description: Audits of agent benchmarks and environments for exploitable verifiers, datasets of hack trajectories, and methods to harden graders and preserve benchmark validity against reward hacking.

categories.name: Misuse, Jailbreaks and Adversarial Robustness
categories.description: Work on attacks against and defenses for LLM safeguards: jailbreaks, prompt injection, fine-tuning/tampering attacks on open weights, agent misuse and unsafe agent behavior, dangerous-capability (e.g. bio) misuse, and automated red teaming.

categories.name: Tamper Resistance and Capability Removal
categories.description: Making safety or capability removal robust to fine-tuning, abliteration and weight modification (pretraining data filtering, modular/MoE knowledge isolation, tamper benchmarks), plus fine-tuning attacks that erode alignment and theoretical limits of behavioral evaluation for certifying post-update safety.

categories.name: Prompt Injection in Agents
categories.description: Attacks on and defenses against prompt injection and instruction-hierarchy violations in LLM agents, including indirect injection via tools, skill files, memory poisoning, role confusion mechanisms, and adversarial training or architectural defenses.

categories.name: Jailbreaks and Safeguard Classifiers
categories.description: Jailbreak attacks on chat models and production classifier safeguards (e.g. Constitutional Classifiers, Rapid Response), jailbreak tax, prefill attacks, and methodology for measuring attack success and safeguard robustness, including LLM-judge reliability and leaderboards.

categories.name: Unsafe Behavior of Deployed Agents
categories.description: Red-teaming and benchmarks showing agents (computer-use, coding, phone, robot, memory-equipped) take harmful or out-of-scope actions, including from benign instructions, prior history, errors, or workflow-level decomposition where chat refusals fail to transfer.

categories.name: Biosecurity and Capability Uplift Misuse
categories.description: Evaluating and mitigating dangerous-capability misuse, especially biology: novice uplift studies, bio-capability benchmarks and red-teaming, biosecurity monitors, and attacks that extract or launder harmful capabilities from safeguarded models into others.

categories.name: AI-Automated Red Teaming
categories.description: Using AI agents or trained models to automatically discover novel jailbreak and prompt injection attacks, and using them for adversarial training of frontier models.

categories.name: Scheming, Evaluation Awareness, and Training Gaming
categories.description: Empirical and conceptual work on whether AI models covertly pursue misaligned goals, recognise and game evaluations or training, and how to measure such propensities validly. Includes scheming/shutdown-resistance propensity evals, evaluation awareness measurement and mitigation, and alignment faking or training-resistance studies.

categories.name: Scheming and Loss-of-Control Propensity Evals
categories.description: Benchmarks, honeypots, and frameworks measuring whether LLM agents actually choose to scheme, sabotage, pursue instrumental goals, resist shutdown, or fail corrigibility in agentic settings, plus critiques of the evidence base for loss-of-control and shutdownability proposals.

categories.name: Measuring and Probing Evaluation Awareness
categories.description: Work characterising, detecting, or steering models' recognition that they are being tested (or who the user is), via verbalised CoT, logits, probes, steering vectors, or model organisms, and quantifying how this awareness shifts measured safety behaviour.

categories.name: Alignment Faking and Training Gaming
categories.description: Studies of models strategically behaving differently under training versus deployment to shape their own updates: alignment faking, exploration/gradient/generalization hacking, reward laundering, and RL amplifying oversight-conditional behaviour.

categories.name: Realistic Deployment-Like Evaluations
categories.description: Methods and benchmarks for making evaluations indistinguishable from real deployment or simulating deployment pre-release (e.g., replaying live usage, deployment scaffolds) to counter evaluation awareness and better predict real-world behaviour rates.

categories.name: Metagaming in Frontier Models
categories.description: Case reports of specific frontier or open-weight models showing metagaming, honeypot-gaming, heightened situational awareness, or worse behaviour when eval-aware, often observed in training runs or model releases.

categories.name: AI Control and Agent Monitoring
categories.description: Research on AI control: monitoring, red-teaming, and protocols that prevent potentially misaligned or adversarial AI agents from causing harm, covering deployed monitoring systems, monitor benchmarks, control protocols, evaluation settings, and multi-agent or distributed attacks.

categories.name: Deployed Lab Monitoring Red-Teaming
categories.description: Work on real-world monitoring and blocking systems at frontier AI companies, including lab control roadmaps, descriptions of internal agent monitoring, red-teaming of production blocking monitors (Auto Mode, Auto-review), and agent threats to oversight such as trace tampering, monitor evasion, or continual learning that undermines blocking monitors.

categories.name: LLM Monitor Benchmarks and Evasion
categories.description: Benchmarks, attack datasets, and empirical studies of how well LLM-based monitors detect sabotage or scheming in agent transcripts. Covers information access, context length, transfer across model families, OOD failures, trained monitors, and adversarial transcript-editing attacks.

categories.name: Control Protocols and Untrusted Monitoring
categories.description: Design and analysis of control protocols and red-team strategies, including attack selection, untrusted monitoring and collusion, resampling and retrying, untrusted advice, bootstrapped monitoring, intervention awareness, authorization delegation, and alignment of monitors themselves.

categories.name: Control Evaluation Settings and Methodology
categories.description: New environments and methods for running control evaluations, such as LinuxArena, Control OSWorld, and simulated control evaluations. Also covers mathematical models of monitor safety curves used to extrapolate eval results to deployment.

categories.name: Distributed and Multi-Agent Attacks
categories.description: Control and detection of attacks spread across many traces, sessions, accounts, or colluding agents. Includes stateful or cross-trace monitoring, persistent-state codebases, insider-threat detection in lab accounts, and multi-agent loss-of-control red-teaming.

categories.name: Interpretability methods, foundations, and estimation
categories.description: Research on understanding neural network internals and generalization: mechanistic estimation and explanation agendas, training-data/generalization structure (SLT-style), critiques and evaluations of SAEs/circuit methods, and geometric or neuron-basis feature representations.

categories.name: ARC mechanistic estimation and parameter decomposition
categories.description: ARC-style work on mechanistic explanations and estimating expectations or rare-event/tail probabilities of network outputs more efficiently than sampling, plus parameter-decomposition approaches to interpreting model weights and small uninterpreted model benchmarks.

categories.name: Data-driven generalization and susceptibility
categories.description: Work linking training data to learned structure and generalization, e.g. Timaeus-style susceptibility 'spectroscopy', patterning (choosing data to induce generalization), scaling/capacity explanations, and deep learning as program synthesis, including org agendas for scaling such alignment science.

categories.name: Faithfulness critiques of interpretability tools
categories.description: Papers testing whether SAEs, activation patching, sparse circuits, and neuron-level explanations actually identify faithful, causally reliable features—random baselines, intervention unreliability, mediator interactions, layer self-correction, and rebuttals that networks are not cleanly interpretable.

categories.name: Neural geometry and neuron-basis features
categories.description: Work on multidimensional and manifold-structured representations (circular number features, concept manifolds, block-sparse featurizers, manifold steering, generative activation models) and the claim that individual neurons already form an interpretable basis.

categories.name: Multi-agent risks and AI social influence
categories.description: Research on misalignment that emerges from AI interacting with other agents or humans: collusion and covert coordination among LLM agents, sycophancy and manipulation of users, conflicts between principals, and strategic bargaining and cooperation between AI agents.

categories.name: Multi-agent collusion and emergent misalignment
categories.description: Evaluations, detection, and mitigation of misaligned behaviour arising in LLM multi-agent systems, such as collusion, steganographic covert communication, peer-preservation, coercion between agents, and misaligned goals or reward hacking that propagate across agents.

categories.name: Sycophancy, persuasion, and user manipulation
categories.description: Studies of how AI assistants affect human users through sycophancy, harmful manipulation, persuasion, political bias, or disempowerment, covering mechanistic circuits behind sycophancy, behavioural evaluations, and human-subject experiments on downstream effects.

categories.name: Competing principals and covert value influence
categories.description: Work on how models resolve conflicts between users, deployers, and their own values, including principal hierarchies, undisclosed value leakage into answers, deception under conflicting incentives, and agents distorting markets to serve their goals.

categories.name: AI bargaining and game-theoretic cooperation
categories.description: Game-theoretic and conceptual analyses of strategic interaction between AI agents, such as bargaining with credible commitments, cooperation via similarity inference, and emergent communication in multi-agent commerce.
